nodes.label: Multinational Corporations (MNCs)
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Companies that own or control production in more than one nation. Set up in regions with cheap labour and resources to minimise costs and maximise profits. Many top MNCs have wealth exceeding entire budgets of developing countries. Control production through joint ventures, local suppliers, or buying up local companies.

nodes.label: Special Economic Zones (SEZs)
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: Industrial zones with world-class facilities (electricity, water, roads, transport, storage). Companies in SEZs get tax exemptions for initial 5 years. Government also allows labour law flexibility. Aims to attract foreign investment. Some opposition due to land acquisition and labour concerns.

nodes.label: Labour Laws and Flexibility
nodes.subject: economics
nodes.detail: To attract foreign investment, government has allowed companies to ignore many worker protection rules. Companies hire workers 'flexibly' for short periods instead of regular basis to reduce labour costs. Foreign companies continue demanding more flexibility. Raises concerns about worker exploitation.
